name: T4 bacteriophage
short_description: The classic docking-apparatus phage: a prolate icosahedral head (~120x86 nm) packed with DNA sits on a neck attached to a contractile tail with a hexagonal baseplate, six kinked long tail fibres gripping Escherichia coli like landing legs, and six short fibres folded up beneath. Naked protein, no envelope.

textbook.1: PARTIAL - correct muted educational cutaway (elongated faceted prolate head, coiled DNA, collar, two-layer tail, hexagonal baseplate); FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: only 5 of 6 long tail fibres clearly resolvable as distinct kinked legs with a foot (grid-overlay + endpoint count on the raw PNG). Re-rendered.
textbook.2: PASS - same house style; FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: annotated all 6 leg-tip (foot) endpoints directly on the raw PNG (see t4-bacteriophage.render.md verification log) - six distinct long kinked fibres confirmed, plus a separate cluster of ~5 short unkinked stubs folded against the baseplate. No lipid envelope, no contracted/star baseplate, no baked text, fills frame edge-to-edge on charcoal background, no duplicate specimen. Chosen as label base (svg_theme).

sem.1: FAIL - style and single-fibre-kink anatomy correct, but a SECOND phage particle (legs + partial tail) is visible out-of-focus in the top-right background corner - violates single-specimen framing. Not usable regardless of its fibre count.
sem.2: PARTIAL (accepted with recorded compromise) - single specimen confirmed (no duplicate), photorealistic false-colour surface-only SEM (correctly no internal cutaway), tail sheath ring texture visible, hexagonal baseplate, no baked text/scale bar, fills frame edge-to-edge on dark substrate. FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: annotated every leg-tip endpoint directly on the raw PNG - only 4 of 6 long tail fibres are clearly resolvable as distinct long kinked legs with a foot; the other two positions are occupied by short, unkinked stubs indistinguishable from the short-tail-fibre cluster (most likely fibres foreshortened toward/away from the camera in this particular pose). A third attempt with an explicit 'six clock positions, none foreshortened' instruction was queued but blocked by the account's MONTHLY SPENDING CAP (confirmed on both gemini-3-pro-image and gemini-2.5-flash-image, not a per-model daily quota) before it could run. Kept as the best available single-specimen SEM; the 4-of-6 count is a real, recorded shortfall, not corrected.

3d.1: PASS - natural biological tints (translucent pale-blue prolate faceted head, golden coiled DNA, grey collar, teal ringed sheath over a paler tube, navy hexagonal baseplate, bronze-tan fibres), single specimen, no envelope, no text, fills frame edge-to-edge on dark studio background. FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: annotated all 6 leg-tip endpoints directly on the raw PNG - six distinct long kinked fibres confirmed, plus a folded short-fibre cluster at the baseplate. Chosen.
3d.2: PARTIAL - re-rendered with an explicit six-clock-position instruction to see if it also fixed 3d; result was single-specimen and correctly styled but FIBRE COUNT MEASURED at only 4 of 6 clearly resolvable long fibres (same foreshortening pattern as sem attempt 2). Attempt 1 was already better on this measure, so attempt 1 was kept instead and this attempt was not used as the label base.

watercolor.1: PASS - warm aged paper fills the entire frame edge-to-edge with a soft darker wash halo directly on the paper (no mat/sheet-on-surface), fine ink linework, single specimen, elongated faceted prolate head with painterly DNA cutaway, no envelope, no text. FIBRE COUNT MEASURED: annotated all 6 leg-tip endpoints directly on the raw PNG - six distinct long kinked fibres confirmed, plus a folded short-fibre cluster. Chosen.
watercolor.2: PARTIAL - re-rendered with the explicit six-clock-position instruction; single-specimen and correctly styled but FIBRE COUNT MEASURED at only 4 of 6 clearly resolvable long fibres, same foreshortening pattern as sem/3d attempt 2. Attempt 1 was already better on this measure and was kept instead.

reference: PASS - real negative-stain TEM of a single isolated T4 virion (Wikimedia Commons, 7USSR7, CC BY 4.0): bright polygonal (prolate) head, straight tail, and a spray of thin fibres at the tail base against a dark stained background. No baked-in caption/scale bar/border; used unedited (nothing to clean). Fibre count is NOT fully resolvable in this micrograph - about 4 of the 6 long tail fibres are distinguishable as separate lines, the rest lost to grain noise/overlap; the six-fibre figure used throughout the renders comes from the structural literature (see render.md Sec 1 sources), not from counting this photograph. The composite 'T4_phage.jpg' pairing the same photo with a labelled schematic diagram was considered and rejected as a reference for exactly that baked-diagram reason.
decision: 6/6 long tail fibres confirmed by endpoint annotation on the raw PNG; correct prolate head, collar, two-layer tail, hexagonal baseplate; no envelope; no text/border

PASS on gemini-2.5-flash-image, first attempt, once the billing cap was raised. Friendly moon-lander-shaped phage character with six short blunt rounded landing-leg bumps (not spikes, no starburst) touching down on a smiling E. coli-planet character, handing a rolled DNA scroll through an already-open hatch; no fight, no bursting. MEASURED EDGE BLEED on the FINAL composed page (cairosvg render of t4-bacteriophage.coloring.svg at 800px, top 72% = the artwork area, outer 6px ink fraction, threshold 128): top 0.0000 -- not a defect, unreachable by construction, since the speech bubble sits in the page's top margin with white space above it on every coloring page in the atlas (confirmed project-wide across all 119 pages, see SKILL.md); bottom 0.107, left 0.041, right 0.023 -- genuine bleed on the three reachable edges, none of them a continuous full-length line (so this is artwork bleed, not an accidental frame). No baked-in text, no starburst on the six leg bumps (confirmed by direct view), speech bubble overlaps the artwork with the tail leaning inward per the coloring-page convention. CORRECTED 2026-08-23: an earlier version of this verdict measured the raw pre-composite PNG instead of the final page and claimed 'bleeds off all 4 edges' -- that claim conflated the artwork's own top row (which does carry a little ink) with the final page's top edge (which is always white margin above the speech bubble, by construction). Left both readings here rather than silently deleting the wrong one.
